issue_context.title: Lack of documentation for `OrthographicProjection`
issue_context.body:
## How can Bevy's documentation be improved?
Add documentation for `OrthographicProjection`.  
As mentioned in [my Discord message](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/742884593551802431/1013296106400129104) there is no official documentation for `OrthographicProjection`, even in `projection.rs`, the first place I looked.

## Why the documentation is "not correct".
[`OrthographicProjection` is in `bevy::render::camera`](https://docs.rs/bevy/0.7.0/bevy/render/camera/struct.OrthographicProjection.html) and has no documentation.  
For example I use [this YouTube video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WnUzWuaMzuM) for reference, and when copying the camera system they use at [05:50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WnUzWuaMzuM&t=350), I want to actually understand what the following code does:  
```rust
cam.orthographic_projection.bottom = -1.;
cam.orthographic_projection.right  = 1.;
cam.orthographic_projection.left   = -1. * RESOLUTION;
cam.orthographic_projection.top    = 1. * RESOLUTION;

// I know what N * RESOLUTION does, but what do the numbers (for `projection.{direction}`) mean?
```

## Suggestions for the new documentation.
I feel like the added documentation should discuss what `OrthographicProjection` is, how it is used, what its properties do, and provide some examples of how to use it.  
Pretty standard, I know, but some people may say "BuT tHis TyPe DoEsN't NeED DocUMeNtATiOn B-BECauSe".

## Help me.
On a side note, if we dig deeper into `scaling_mode` we see the term "world unit" but the documentation doesn't make it clear what that term is defined as.  
If you'd like to help explain to me what any of these are so I can make my game in peace, knowing exactly what everything is doing, check out the [Discord thread I made](https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/1013296106400129104) for it in [the Bevy guild](https://discord.com/invite/bevy).
comments:
Also I'm reporting this for Bevy `^0.7` so I'd like if those versions of the docs could be updated so I'm not mislead by possibly newer specifications.  
I doubt there are any for this specific type, but it would be good QoL since I made the Issue for that version **and** `^0.7` is literally the previous Bevy update, so it's not like you're adding documentation to a historic version of the library.

review_comments: I used "cross sectional area" here since just "size" or "area" is a bit ambiguous and might refer to volume/surface area.

Wow, thank you for looking into this! This is so much clearer.

Can you clarify the following? 

```
    /// When resizing the window, object in the center of the screen remain in the center, while opposite
    /// faces of the view frustum expand/shrink equally.
``` 

I understand, that in contrast to `BottomLeft`, which keeps the bottom and left faces fixed, this will change all the faces equally to perform the scaling operation. But I am not sure I understand the significance of "objects in the center of the screen remain in the center".

What happens to objects at the center of the screen when using `BottomLeft`?

Is there any way for the width/height of the view frustum to be different than the width/height of the window? The only case I can think of is if `scaling_mode` is `None`, but then contents in the view frustum will just be stretched to fill the window.

@xgbwei Will the contents just be stretched to fit the window? I thought some things will just lie outside the window if the view frustrum is larger than the window, for example (and thus those objects will not be visible)?

> Is there any way for the width/height of the view frustum to be different than the width/height of the window? The only case I can think of is if `scaling_mode` is `None`, but then contents in the view frustum will just be stretched to fill the window.

The `viewport` field on the camera allows you to specify custom viewport dimensions, for things like multiple views. In my tiled camera crate I use it to force the game view to a multiple of some target resolution to avoid pixel artifacts when rendering low resolution images.

To make this a proper adoption of the previous PR, please include the documentation for `WindowOrigin` ~~and `ScalingMode`~~ that the previous PR included. 

If the documentation in the previous PR wasn't sufficient (I don't think it was), this should be improved, not removed.
I felt that the previous explanations were a bit redundant. I'll try to add some examples here but I'll have to play around with `WindowOrigin` a bit more.
@xgbwei I found from Discord: `WindowOrigin` specifies where the world space `(0, 0)` is relative to the Window.

> @xgbwei I found from Discord: `WindowOrigin` specifies where the world space `(0, 0)` is relative to the Window.

I've looked at the implementation and this isn't accurate. Check the new docs for `WindowOrigin`.
